text:
Mikko Rantanen became the fourth Finnish player to reach 800 NHL points this month, joining Teemu Selanne, Jari Kurri and Saku Koivu, and he got there in style: 14 points over his last ten games, including a three-goal night against Boston and goals in three straight.

This is the season Dallas paid for. The Stars get 58% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, and he's 11 points better than his teammates by that measure. He's 19th of 515 skaters in wins added by goals.

The finishing is the warning light. He has 9 goals on 5.3 expected, shooting 27% after 16% last season, and only 33 shots in 17 games. That rate doesn't survive a full season, and our range for his shooting is 13 to 18%. His ice time has also dipped about a minute and a half lately. None of that is a knock on the player: carry-ins on 56% of his entries, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, are the kind of habit that keeps a top line moving. Watch the shot count, not the goals.
headline: Rantanen reaches 800, and the shots keep dropping
